scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with an iceberg. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 61 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. However, the ocean water is quite cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly get hypothermia.
choice: I decide to physically throw 10 passengers from lifeboat B overboard
entities: I,other occupants of Lifeboat A,10 passengers in Lifeboat B who would be thrown overboard,51 remaining occupants of Lifeboat B
outcomes: Ten passengers are in the cold ocean water
Ten passengers suffer severe fear and distress
Lifeboat B has ten fewer people aboard
Lifeboat B is no longer dangerously overcrowded
The remaining people in Lifeboat B avoid the immediate danger of the lifeboat sinking from overload
Passengers and crew who witness the event experience shock and distress
